Subject: Performance SLOs & Benchmark methodology — FinEdge discovery

Hi Jordan / Anika —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re aligned on the SLO work and the benchmark handoff: 

Recap of core SLO asks you mentioned:
- 95th percentile latency < 250ms for single-stream interactive chat at 512 tokens (including streaming start latency)
- Sustained throughput target: 100 QPS average, with spikes up to 300 QPS for short bursts
- Concurrent session goal: support 300 concurrent active sessions with KV cache warmup behavior accounted for
- Streaming semantics: server-sent events for partial tokens and immediate first-token delivery <= 100ms where possible

What we propose from Redwood for an initial reproducible benchmark: 
1) Prompt set: you’ll provide a representative sample from your production prompt set (we discussed 1k samples to start). We’ll validate format.
2) Eval harness: we’ll run a closed harness (no external calls) with deterministic seeds and your traffic mix. We’ll publish raw logs and summarized percentiles.
3) Measurement definitions: clear definitions for "first-token latency", "stream-start latency", "p95/p99 tail", and how batching affects per-request latency.
4) Repro steps: exact model version, quantization profile, instance type, kernel flags, and a Docker image tag so you can re-run locally.

Next steps I propose:
- Jordan: share the 1k prompt sample + a short doc describing traffic mix and any special streaming requirements (e.g., stop tokens, partial output merging).
- Dylan (cc’d): I’ve looped in our SE to scope the harness and confirm the perf measurement outputs we’ll share.
- We’ll aim to do an initial run by EOD next Wednesday (Mar 4) if we receive prompts & sample config by EOD this Friday.

Attachments: perf-run-config.yaml (YAML) — small template for how to format the traffic mix.

If that looks good I’ll kick off the internal task and set a calendar for a short run-planning sync (30m).

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and mostly aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and items we’ll attach: 

Clarifications:
- The 250ms p95 target is for typical short-turn dialog (avg response length ~40 tokens). For longer responses we expect higher tail times; please surface median vs p95 separately.
- For streaming: first-token <=100ms is critical for UI snappiness. We’re willing to accept slightly higher total completion latency if streaming start is low.
- Concurrency: 300 concurrent "active" sessions means sessions with an open stream; some sessions will be idle but pinned. Please include cold-start numbers if applicable.

We will attach a 1,000-sample prompt set (anonymized) and a short doc describing traffic mix and average response length per bucket. Attaching: finedge_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (JSONL, 1k lines), traffic-mix.md (doc).

One ask on measurement reproducibility: when you publish raw logs, can you include the exact container image digest and the kernel flags used (we want to reproduce the run in our staging). Also include a small script that replays the harness against a local model variant.

Happy for Dylan to coordinate the exact harness inputs. If you can confirm the run window next Wed (UTC-friendly window mid-day PST), we’ll prioritize resources.

—Jordan

Hi Jordan / Marissa —

Thanks — I’m Dylan, SE on the account. Per Marissa’s note I’ve drafted the initial benchmark methodology and a runnable harness plan. Summary below and I’ve attached a short instructions doc you can use to reproduce locally.

Benchmark methodology (high level):
1) Harness overview
   - We’ll use a deterministic harness based on our eval-runner (see repo link below). The harness simulates client behavior and supports both single-request and streaming (chunked) modes.
2) Measurement definitions (explicit)
   - first_token_latency: time from request accept to first token byte emitted on the stream
   - stream_start_latency: time until first SSE/frame is received by the client (includes server push overhead)
   - completion_latency: time to final token emitted (end-of-stream)
   - per-request_tail: p50/p95/p99 computed on completion_latency across the sample set
   - throughput: measured as completed requests per second over 60s windows, reported as average and 95th windowed percentiles

3) Configuration we’ll publish with every run
   - container image digest (sha256)

Thanks Dylan — this is great and the definitions look solid. A couple quick notes:

- Please include guidance on how we measure client-side reassembly latency for streaming chunks (we need to know if your numbers assume client reassembly is instant).
- For reproducibility: adding perf counters (nvprof/perf) is useful but we’re mainly interested in the exact kernel/cudnn/driver versions used.

We’ll schedule the window for Wed Mar 4 at 10:30 PT. I’ll share a calendar invite to the address on this thread (marissa.cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com).

Attaching: traffic-mix.md (doc) and prompt set confirmed. We’ll also provide a small golden-reference output set after your run so we can validate quality regressions.

Looking forward — Jordan
